channel.title: AI Security Paper Digest
channel.description: Curated papers on AI security from ArXiv and ACL

item.title: Metaphor-based Jailbreak Attacks on Text-to-Image Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes metaphor-based jailbreak attacks (MJA) to bypass text-to-image model safety defenses without knowing the deployed defense type.
  • Uses an LLM multi-agent generation module (LMAG) for metaphor retrieval, context matching, and adversarial prompt generation, plus an adversarial prompt optimization module (APO) with a surrogate model and acquisition strategy to reduce queries.
  • Evaluates MJA against multiple external and internal defense mechanisms, reporting stronger and more query-efficient attack performance than several baselines.
  • Provides analysis attributing success to semantic ambiguity from metaphor prompts and probabilistic interpretation leading to sensitive image generation.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Chenyu Zhang', 'Lanjun Wang', 'Yiwen Ma', 'Wenhui Li', 'Yi Tu', 'An-An Liu']
  • Tags: ['jailbreak-attacks', 'prompt-injection-evasion', 'text-to-image-security', 'adversarial-prompts', 'LLM-based-attack-automation']

item.title: Latent Diffusion Inversion Requires Understanding the Latent Space
item.description:
Summary

  • Investigates model inversion/membership inference privacy risks in latent diffusion models (LDMs).
  • Finds non-uniform memorization across latent codes and unequal memorization across latent representation dimensions.
  • Proposes ranking latent dimensions by their contribution to decoder pullback metric and shows removing less-memorizing dimensions improves membership-inference performance.
  • Provides insights linking auto-encoder geometry to diffusion memorization and privacy vulnerabilities.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Mingxing Rao', 'Bowen Qu', 'Daniel Moyer']
  • Tags: ['model inversion', 'membership inference', 'privacy attacks', 'diffusion models', 'latent diffusion']

item.title: Inverting Neural Networks: New Methods to Generate Neural Network Inputs from Prescribed Outputs
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies neural network inversion: generating input images that produce prescribed output classes/scores.
  • Introduces two inversion approaches (root-finding with Jacobian; layer-wise backward inversion with null-space perturbations).
  • Finds that the generated inputs can yield near-perfect classification scores while appearing random-like, indicating exploitable vulnerabilities in the models.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Rebecca Pattichis', 'Sebastian Janampa', 'Constantinos S. Pattichis', 'Marios S. Pattichis']
  • Tags: ['neural-network-inversion', 'privacy-model-leakage', 'adversarial-examples', 'transformers', 'security-vulnerabilities']

item.title: HalDec-Bench: Benchmarking Hallucination Detector in Image Captioning
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces HalDec-Bench to evaluate hallucination detectors for image captioning by testing whether captions correctly align with image content.
  • Provides captions from diverse VLMs with human annotations for hallucination presence, hallucination-type categories, and segment-level labels.
  • Includes interpretable, difficulty-varied tasks and analyzes detector behavior and dataset noise reduction via filtering/caption generation pipeline.

Paper Type

  • Benchmarking/Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Kuniaki Saito', 'Risa Shinoda', 'Shohei Tanaka', 'Tosho Hirasawa', 'Fumio Okura', 'Yoshitaka Ushiku']
  • Tags: ['hallucination detection', 'vision-language models', 'dataset curation', 'benchmarking', 'alignment evaluation']

item.title: DifAttack++: Query-Efficient Black-Box Adversarial Attack via Hierarchical Disentangled Feature Space in Cross-Domain
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes DifAttack++, a query-efficient black-box adversarial attack method using a hierarchical disentangled feature space.
  • Uses an autoencoder framework (HDF) to separate adversarial features (AF) from visual features (VF), optimizing only AF during black-box queries.
  • Trains cross-domain autoencoders with clean images and adversarial examples generated via white-box attacks on surrogate models.
  • Reports improved attack success rate and query efficiency with comparable visual quality of adversarial images.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Jun Liu', 'Jiantao Zhou', 'Jiandian Zeng', 'Jinyu Tian', 'Isao Echizen']
  • Tags: ['black-box adversarial attacks', 'query-efficient attacks', 'adversarial examples', 'feature disentanglement', 'surrogate-model transfer']

item.title: TreeTeaming: Autonomous Red-Teaming of Vision-Language Models via Hierarchical Strategy Exploration
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces TreeTeaming, an autonomous red-teaming framework for vision-language models that explores attack strategies via a dynamically expanded hierarchical strategy tree rather than a fixed linear test set.
  • Uses an LLM-based strategic orchestrator to decide between evolving promising attack paths or branching into new strategy explorations, paired with a multimodal actuator to execute attacks.
  • Evaluates on 12 prominent VLMs and reports state-of-the-art attack success rates on 11 models, including high success against GPT-4o, with improved strategic diversity and stealth metrics (e.g., toxicity reduction).

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Chunxiao Li', 'Lijun Li', 'Jing Shao']
  • Tags: ['automated red teaming', 'jailbreaking', 'vision-language models', 'multimodal attacks', 'strategy exploration']

item.title: SMSP: A Plug-and-Play Strategy of Multi-Scale Perception for MLLMs to Perceive Visual Illusions
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies multimodal large language model (MLLM) vulnerability to hidden-pattern visual illusions where models miss human-imperceptible/hidden content.
  • Identifies a failure mechanism (high-frequency attention bias to background textures) and demonstrates systemic evaluation using a new illusion dataset (IlluChar).
  • Proposes a plug-and-play defense/preprocessing framework (SMSP) that suppresses distracting high-frequency backgrounds to align model perception with humans.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Jinzhe Tu', 'Ruilei Guo', 'Zihan Guo', 'Junxiao Yang', 'Shiyao Cui', 'Minlie Huang']
  • Tags: ['MLLM security', 'visual illusion vulnerability', 'attack/robustness evaluation', 'defense via preprocessing', 'multimodal perception']

item.title: AgentFoX: LLM Agent-Guided Fusion with eXplainability for AI-Generated Image Detection
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes AgentFoX, an LLM-agent framework for detecting AI-generated images via a multi-phase, explainable analysis pipeline.
  • Uses LLM-driven fusion guided by expert knowledge profiles and clustering/context profiles to reconcile conflicting evidence from different forensic cues.
  • Outputs detailed human-readable forensic reports rather than only binary classification, aiming to improve interpretability for deployment.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Yangxin Yu', 'Yue Zhou', 'Bin Li', 'Kaiqing Lin', 'Haodong Li', 'Jiangqun Ni', 'Bo Cao']
  • Tags: ['AI-generated image detection', 'LLM agent', 'Forensics', 'Explainability', 'Multimodal']

item.title: Injecting Falsehoods: Adversarial Man-in-the-Middle Attacks Undermining Factual Recall in LLMs
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces Xmera, a principled adversarial man-in-the-middle (MitM) framework to evaluate how prompt-injection attacks affect LLM factual recall in closed-book QA tasks.
  • Shows that instruction-based MitM attacks can achieve high success rates (up to ~85.3%) while increasing uncertainty on incorrect answers.
  • Proposes a defense using Random Forest classifiers trained on response uncertainty to detect attacked vs. unattacked queries (up to ~94.8% AUC).

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Alina Fastowski', 'Bardh Prenkaj', 'Yuxiao Li', 'Gjergji Kasneci']
  • Tags: ['prompt injection', 'man-in-the-middle (MitM) attacks', 'LLM factual recall', 'uncertainty-based detection', 'adversarial security evaluation']

item.title: RedTopic: Toward Topic-Diverse Red Teaming of Large Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes RedTopic, a framework for topic-diverse red teaming of large language models using a contextualized prompt generation pipeline.
  • Introduces an aggregate reward design and multi-objective RL training loop to improve exploration and maintain adversarial topic diversity.
  • Demonstrates improved effectiveness and diversity of adversarial prompts versus existing red teaming approaches on integrated evaluation metrics.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Jiale Ding', 'Xiang Zheng', 'Yutao Wu', 'Cong Wang', 'Wei-Bin Lee', 'Ling Pan', 'Xingjun Ma', 'Yu-Gang Jiang']
  • Tags: ['red teaming', 'LLM safety evaluation', 'adversarial prompting', 'RL-based adversarial prompt generation']

item.title: DualEdit: Mitigating Safety Fallback in LLM Backdoor Editing via Affirmation-Refusal Regulation
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies backdoor attacks and instability in safety-aligned LLM model editing ("safety fallback").
  • Proposes DualEdit, a model-editing framework to improve mapping from triggers to attacker-desired behaviors while regulating refusal generation.
  • Introduces dynamic loss weighting and value anchoring to stabilize optimization and reduce conflicts from diverse refusal behaviors.
  • Reports improved attack success and reduced fallback rate in experiments on safety-aligned LLMs.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Houcheng Jiang', 'Zetong Zhao', 'Junfeng Fang', 'Haokai Ma', 'Ruipeng Wang', 'Xiang Wang', 'Xiangnan He', 'Yang Deng']
  • Tags: ['LLM backdoors', 'model editing attacks', 'safety alignment bypass', 'adversarial optimization', 'refusal manipulation']

item.title: T-MAP: Red-Teaming LLM Agents with Trajectory-aware Evolutionary Search
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes T-MAP, a trajectory-aware evolutionary search red-teaming method for LLM agents
  • Uses multi-step tool execution trajectories to generate adversarial prompts that bypass safety guardrails and achieve harmful objectives
  • Evaluates across multiple MCP (Model Context Protocol) environments and shows higher attack realization rate than baselines
  • Demonstrates effectiveness against frontier models, uncovering agent-specific vulnerabilities

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Hyomin Lee', 'Sangwoo Park', 'Yumin Choi', 'Sohyun An', 'Seanie Lee', 'Sung Ju Hwang']
  • Tags: ['LLM security', 'Red teaming', 'Agent/tool-use attacks', 'Trajectory-aware search', 'MCP']

item.title: Detecting Non-Membership in LLM Training Data via Rank Correlations
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes PRISM, a grey-box test for detecting dataset-level non-membership in LLM training data.
  • Uses rank correlation between models’ normalized token log probabilities to distinguish unseen datasets from seen ones.
  • Aims to rule out training membership while avoiding false positives across multiple datasets.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Pranav Shetty', 'Mirazul Haque', 'Zhiqiang Ma', 'Xiaomo Liu']
  • Tags: ['privacy', 'membership inference', 'training data extraction/non-membership', 'LLM security evaluation']

item.title: Impact of Positional Encoding: Clean and Adversarial Rademacher Complexity for Transformers under In-Context Regression
item.description:
Summary

  • Analyzes how trainable positional encoding (PE) affects clean generalization in a single-layer Transformer for in-context regression.
  • Derives adversarial generalization bounds using adversarial Rademacher complexity, explicitly comparing models with and without PE.
  • Finds that PE increases the clean generalization gap and that the gap is further magnified under adversarial conditions, indicating higher vulnerability.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Weiyi He', 'Yue Xing']
  • Tags: ['adversarial generalization', 'positional encoding', 'Rademacher complexity', 'in-context learning (ICL)', 'theoretical security/robustness']

item.title: CyberGym: Evaluating AI Agents' Real-World Cybersecurity Capabilities at Scale
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces CyberGym, a large-scale benchmark to evaluate AI agents’ real-world cybersecurity capabilities.
  • Tests agents on generating proof-of-concept tests to reproduce vulnerabilities from text descriptions and codebases.
  • Finds that overall success rates are low (~20%), indicating substantial challenge and differentiation across systems.
  • Reports real-world impact by discovering 34 zero-day vulnerabilities and 18 incomplete patches.

Paper Type

  • Benchmarking

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Zhun Wang', 'Tianneng Shi', 'Jingxuan He', 'Matthew Cai', 'Jialin Zhang', 'Dawn Song']
  • Tags: ['cybersecurity benchmarking', 'vulnerability reproduction', 'AI agents', 'red teaming/evaluation', 'proof-of-concept testing']

item.title: Leakage and Interpretability in Concept-Based Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes an information-theoretic framework to quantify “information leakage” in concept-based (interpretable) models via two metrics: concepts-task leakage (CTL) and interconcept leakage (ICL).
  • Demonstrates that CTL/ICL scores predict model behavior under interventions and outperform existing leakage measures.
  • Identifies main causes of leakage and analyzes leakage types (including alignment/interconcept leakage) in specific concept embedding model variants.
  • Provides practical design guidelines to reduce leakage and improve interpretability in concept-based models.

Paper Type

  • Research Paper

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Enrico Parisini', 'Tapabrata Chakraborti', 'Chris Harbron', 'Ben D. MacArthur', 'Christopher R. S. Banerji']
  • Tags: ['model interpretability', 'information leakage', 'concept-based models', 'information-theoretic analysis', 'intervention-based evaluation']

item.title: Not All Tokens Are Created Equal: Query-Efficient Jailbreak Fuzzing for LLMs
item.description:
Summary

  • Analyzes how individual tokens contribute unevenly to LLM refusal behavior during jailbreak attempts.
  • Proposes TriageFuzz, a token-aware jailbreak fuzzing framework using a surrogate model to estimate token-level refusal contributions.
  • Uses a refusal-guided evolutionary strategy to steer prompt mutation toward policy-bypassing outputs under strict query budgets.
  • Experiments on multiple open-source LLMs and commercial APIs show similar or better jailbreak success rates with substantially fewer queries.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Wenyu Chen', 'Xiangtao Meng', 'Chuanchao Zang', 'Li Wang', 'Xinyu Gao', 'Jianing Wang', 'Peng Zhan', 'Zheng Li', 'Shanqing Guo']
  • Tags: ['Jailbreaks', 'Fuzzing', 'LLM Safety Evasion', 'Query-Efficient Attacks', 'Refusal Behavior Analysis']

item.title: Robust Safety Monitoring of Language Models via Activation Watermarking
item.description:
Summary

  • Frames robust LLM safety monitoring as an adversarial security game against adaptive attackers.
  • Demonstrates that existing LLM monitoring approaches can be evaded by attackers aware of the monitoring mechanism.
  • Proposes improved defenses using activation watermarking to introduce uncertainty and make evasion harder without knowing the secret key.
  • Reports improved detection performance over guard baselines under adaptive adversaries.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Toluwani Aremu', 'Daniil Ognev', 'Samuele Poppi', 'Nils Lukas']
  • Tags: ['LLM safety monitoring', 'Adaptive adversarial attacks', 'Detection/defense', 'Activation watermarking', 'Security game']

item.title: A Critical Review on the Effectiveness and Privacy Threats of Membership Inference Attacks
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes an evaluation framework to determine when membership inference attacks (MIAs) are a genuine privacy threat.
  • Reviews representative MIAs using the proposed conditions and assesses their real-world effectiveness.
  • Concludes that, under realistic assumptions, MIAs are weak threats, so MIAs may overstate privacy risk if used as a primary metric.

Paper Type

  • Survey/Review

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Najeeb Jebreel', "David S\\'anchez", 'Josep Domingo-Ferrer']
  • Tags: ['privacy vulnerability', 'membership inference', 'evaluation framework', 'threat modeling', 'privacy attacks']

item.title: Privacy-Preserving Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback via Decoupled Reward Modeling
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a privacy-preserving RLHF pipeline by applying differential privacy only during reward modeling (reward learning), then deriving the final policy from the resulting private reward model.
  • Provides theoretical analysis including suboptimality gaps and minimax lower bounds, showing how privacy introduces additional error terms and changes dominant sample-size/privacy regimes.
  • Empirically validates the scaling behavior on synthetic data and reports improved private alignment on the Anthropic HH-RLHF dataset using Gemma-2B-IT versus DP baselines.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Young Hyun Cho', 'Will Wei Sun']
  • Tags: ['privacy', 'differential privacy', 'RLHF', 'reward modeling', 'privacy-preserving ML']

item.title: OrgForge-IT: A Verifiable Synthetic Benchmark for LLM-Based Insider Threat Detection
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces OrgForge-IT, a verifiable synthetic benchmark for LLM-based insider threat detection with deterministic ground truth.
  • Designs multiple detection scenarios (four) across threat classes and injectable behaviors to defeat single-surface/single-day triage strategies.
  • Includes scoring and analysis focused on triage vs verdict accuracy, false-positive rates, attribution errors, temporal correlation across multi-day telemetry, and prompt sensitivity/hallucinations.
  • Provides a multi-model leaderboard and reports performance differences tied to model scale and training regimes.

Paper Type

  • Benchmarking

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Jeffrey Flynt']
  • Tags: ['insider threat detection', 'synthetic benchmarks', 'LLM evaluation', 'security testing', 'telemetry triage']

item.title: SafeSeek: Universal Attribution of Safety Circuits in Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes SafeSeek, a unified mechanistic interpretability framework to identify safety-critical functional components (“safety circuits”) in LLMs.
  • Uses differentiable binary masks and optimization on safety datasets to extract multi-granular circuits reliably across settings.
  • Validates on backdoor attack attribution (ablation removes near-100% ASR while preserving utility) and on safety alignment circuit localization (removal greatly increases ASR).
  • Integrates extracted circuits via Safety Circuit Tuning for efficient safety fine-tuning.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Miao Yu', 'Siyuan Fu', 'Moayad Aloqaily', 'Zhenhong Zhou', 'Safa Otoum', 'Xing fan', 'Kun Wang', 'Yufei Guo', 'Qingsong Wen']
  • Tags: ['mechanistic interpretability', 'backdoor attacks', 'safety alignment', 'model security defenses', 'circuit attribution']

item.title: Precision-Varying Prediction (PVP): Robustifying ASR systems against adversarial attacks
item.description:
Summary

  • Study adversarial robustness of automatic speech recognition (ASR) models against adversarial attacks.
  • Propose Precision-Varying Prediction (PVP), which randomly varies inference precision to reduce attack success rates.
  • Introduce an adversarial example detection approach based on discrepancies across outputs from different precisions.
  • Show improved robustness and competitive detection performance across multiple ASR models and attack types.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ["Mat\\'ias Pizarro", 'Raghavan Narasimhan', 'Asja Fischer']
  • Tags: ['Adversarial Attacks', 'Adversarial Detection', 'ASR Robustness', 'Model Inference Defenses']

item.title: Adversarial Vulnerabilities in Neural Operator Digital Twins: Gradient-Free Attacks on Nuclear Thermal-Hydraulic Surrogates
item.description:
Summary

  • Investigates adversarial robustness of neural operator digital twin surrogates for nuclear thermal-hydraulic prediction.
  • Demonstrates gradient-free, extremely sparse (<1% of inputs) physically plausible perturbations on boundary conditions that cause catastrophic prediction errors.
  • Shows standard validation/anomaly detection can fail entirely (100% of successful single-point attacks evade z-score anomaly detection).
  • Introduces an effective perturbation dimension diagnostic to explain architecture-dependent exploitability and compares gradient-free vs gradient-based attack effectiveness.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Samrendra Roy', 'Kazuma Kobayashi', 'Souvik Chakraborty', 'Rizwan-uddin', 'Syed Bahauddin Alam']
  • Tags: ['adversarial attacks', 'gradient-free optimization', 'robustness evaluation', 'digital twins/neural operators']

item.title: Sample Transform Cost-Based Training-Free Hallucination Detector for Large Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a training-free hallucination detector for LLMs using optimal-transport/Wasserstein distances between token-embedding sets from multiple sampled responses per prompt.
  • Derives two signals from the Wasserstein distance matrix: AvgWD (average transform cost) and EigenWD (cost complexity).
  • Extends to black-box settings using teacher forcing with an accessible teacher model.
  • Evaluates against uncertainty baselines, framing hallucination detection as a truthfulness/security-related reliability problem.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Zeyang Ding', 'Xinglin Hu', 'Jicong Fan']
  • Tags: ['LLM hallucination detection', 'truthfulness evaluation', 'optimal transport/Wasserstein distance', 'training-free detection', 'black-box adaptation']

item.title: DeepXplain: XAI-Guided Autonomous Defense Against Multi-Stage APT Campaigns
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes DeepXplain, an explainable deep reinforcement learning framework for autonomous defense against multi-stage APTs.
  • Uses provenance-based graph learning and temporal stage estimation to determine the current attack stage and guide defense actions.
  • Integrates explanation signals into policy optimization via evidence alignment and confidence-aware reward shaping, aiming for more trustworthy decisions in operational environments.
  • Evaluated in a realistic enterprise testbed with reported gains in stage-weighted detection/defense metrics and explanation quality (confidence, fidelity, compactness).

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Trung V. Phan', 'Thomas Bauschert']
  • Tags: ['APT defense', 'Explainable reinforcement learning', 'Cybersecurity intrusion detection', 'Graph-based provenance modeling', 'Defense automation']

item.title: Agent Control Protocol: Admission Control for Agent Actions
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes an Agent Control Protocol (ACP) as an admission-control layer that cryptographically authorizes autonomous agent actions before execution.
  • Uses capability-based authorization, identity verification, delegation chains with transitive revocation, deterministic risk evaluation, and immutable cryptographically-chained auditing.
  • Includes formal verification via a TLA+ model (stated invariants with no violations) and conformance testing with signed/unsigned test vectors and stateful sequence compliance.

Paper Type

  • Research/Technical Specification

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Marcelo Fernandez (TraslaIA)']
  • Tags: ['agent security', 'admission control', 'capability-based authorization', 'cryptographic auditing', 'formal verification']

item.title: MCP Security Bench (MSB): Benchmarking Attacks Against Model Context Protocol in LLM Agents
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces MSB, an end-to-end benchmark suite for measuring how LLM agents handle MCP-specific attacks across planning, tool invocation, and response handling.
  • Defines a taxonomy of 12 attack types (e.g., prompt injection in tool descriptions, retrieval injection, name collision, preference manipulation, out-of-scope parameter requests, and false-error escalation).
  • Implements an evaluation harness that executes real (benign and malicious) tools via MCP rather than simulation.
  • Proposes a robustness metric (Net Resilient Performance, NRP) and evaluates multiple LLM agents across many domains/tools, producing thousands of attack instances.

Paper Type

  • Benchmarking

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Dongsen Zhang', 'Zekun Li', 'Xu Luo', 'Xuannan Liu', 'Peipei Li', 'Wenjun Xu']
  • Tags: ['LLM Agents', 'Tool-Use Security', 'Benchmarking', 'Prompt Injection', 'Context Protocol (MCP)']

item.title: Not All Tokens Are Created Equal: Query-Efficient Jailbreak Fuzzing for LLMs

item.title: SafeSeek: Universal Attribution of Safety Circuits in Language Models

item.title: Mind Your HEARTBEAT! Claw Background Execution Inherently Enables Silent Memory Pollution
item.description:
Summary

  • Identifies a security vulnerability in Claw personal AI agents where untrusted content encountered during heartbeat-driven background execution can silently pollute agent memory.
  • Formalizes an Exposure→Memory→Behavior pathway, showing how misinformation can propagate from background ingestion to user-facing downstream behavior without user awareness or provenance.
  • Uses a controlled social-agent replica (MissClaw) to demonstrate high rates of short-term influence and durable long-term memory pollution, including cross-session effects.
  • Finds that prompt injection is not required; ordinary social misinformation can drive the vulnerability via background execution and shared session memory context.

item.title: AgentRAE: Remote Action Execution through Notification-based Visual Backdoors against Screenshots-based Mobile GUI Agents
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes AgentRAE, a backdoor attack targeting screenshots-based mobile GUI agents by using notification visuals (e.g., benign-looking app icons) as triggers.
  • Uses a two-stage training pipeline (contrastive learning to sharpen sensitivity to subtle icon differences, then backdoor post-training for action redirection).
  • Shows high attack success (>90%) across multiple mobile operations while preserving clean performance.
  • Demonstrates resilience against multiple state-of-the-art defenses and highlights a notification-conditioned behavioral vulnerability.

item.title: Sample Transform Cost-Based Training-Free Hallucination Detector for Large Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a training-free hallucination detector for LLMs using optimal-transport/Wasserstein distances between token-embedding sets from multiple sampled responses per prompt.
  • Derives two signals from the Wasserstein distance matrix: AvgWD (average transform cost) and EigenWD (cost complexity).
  • Extends to black-box settings using teacher forcing with an accessible teacher model.
  • Evaluates against uncertainty baselines, framing hallucination detection as a truthfulness/security-related reliability problem.

item.description:

item.title: ProGRank: Probe-Gradient Reranking to Defend Dense-Retriever RAG from Corpus Poisoning
item.description:
Summary

  • ProGRank is a retriever-side, post hoc, training-free defense against corpus poisoning in dense-retriever RAG systems.
  • It uses randomized perturbations to probe stability of query–passage pairs and extracts retriever probe gradients from a small parameter subset.
  • From probe signals it computes instability metrics (representational consistency and dispersion risk) and applies a reranking score gate to suppress poisoned passages.
  • Experiments evaluate against multiple corpus poisoning attacks, showing improved robustness with minimal utility loss, including against adaptive evasive attacks.

item.title: Chain-of-Authorization: Internalizing Authorization into Large Language Models via Reasoning Trajectories

  • Introduces authorization as a causal prerequisite for answering by requiring stages like resource review, identity resolution, and decision-making before generating responses.

item.title: Session Risk Memory (SRM): Temporal Authorization for Deterministic Pre-Execution Safety Gates
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes Session Risk Memory (SRM), a deterministic safety module that adds trajectory-level (temporal) authorization to per-action safety gates.
  • Targets failures where distributed/multi-step attacks decompose harmful intent into individually compliant steps, using a session centroid and accumulated risk signal (EMA over baseline-subtracted gate outputs).
  • Evaluates SRM on a benchmark with slow-burn exfiltration, gradual privilege escalation, and compliance drift across multi-turn sessions, reporting perfect F1 and 0% false positives for ILION+SRM.
  • Emphasizes a distinction between spatial (per-action) and temporal (over-trajectory) authorization consistency for agentic system safety.
